query_text: In August 2024, a job applicant created a fake university degree certificate and submitted it to our company HR department to obtain employment.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S336_E1: Making false document or electronic record
BNS_S336_E2: Intent to deceive or commit fraud to obtain employment
BNS_S340_E2: Using forged document as genuine with knowledge
rationale: Fabricating a counterfeit educational degree and fraudulently submitting it to secure a job constitutes forgery under Section 336 BNS and using a forged document as genuine under Section 340 BNS (governs acts on or after 1 July 2024).
unresolved_ambiguity: Requires human review to determine if BNS 336 alone or both 336+340 should be ground truth.

query_text: In November 2023, an employee fabricated a fake vendor invoice on official company letterhead and submitted it to finance to claim a fraudulent reimbursement.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S468_E1: Forgery of a document
IPC_S468_E2: Intent that forged document be used for cheating
IPC_S471_E2: Fraudulently presenting forged document as genuine
rationale: Historical forgery committed prior to 1 July 2024 for cheating finance constitutes Section 468 IPC and presenting it as genuine constitutes Section 471 IPC under Section 358 BNS savings and Article 20(1).
unresolved_ambiguity: Requires confirmation of IPC 468 vs 465 historical baseline.

query_text: In September 2024, an individual presented a doctored property deed that had been forged by an unknown third party, knowing it was fake, to register a disputed land plot.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S340_E1: Document is forged
BNS_S340_E2: Dishonestly using forged document as genuine with knowledge
rationale: Submitting a forged deed knowing it is fabricated satisfies Section 340 BNS even if the presenter was not the original forger.

query_text: In January 2024, a contractor altered the date and figure on an official clearance certificate to avoid municipal inspection penalties.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S465_E1: Making false document by alteration
IPC_S465_E2: Fraudulent intent to avoid penalties
rationale: Pre-July 2024 general document alteration without cheating a specific person out of property constitutes Section 465 IPC.
unresolved_ambiguity: Review whether municipal fraud entails higher penalties.

query_text: In August 2024, a corporate treasurer was entrusted with company liquid assets but secretly siphoned twenty lakh rupees into a personal cryptocurrency wallet.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S316_E1: Entrustment with company liquid assets
BNS_S316_E2: Dishonest misappropriation and conversion to own use
rationale: Dishonest conversion of entrusted corporate assets to personal digital currency constitutes criminal breach of trust under Section 316 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In March 2024, a warehouse manager entrusted with electronic goods inventory dishonestly sold fifty laptops on the grey market and kept the cash.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S406_E1: Entrustment of electronic inventory
IPC_S406_E2: Dishonest misappropriation and sale for personal gain
rationale: Historical misappropriation of entrusted goods committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 406 IPC.

query_text: In August 2024, a disgruntled ex-employee entered the office server room and intentionally cut the fiber optic cables, destroying critical network equipment.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S324_E1: Intent to cause wrongful loss and destruction
BNS_S324_E2: Destruction of property diminishing utility
ITA_S43_E3: Damaging computer network and equipment
rationale: Physical sabotage of network infrastructure constitutes mischief under Section 324 BNS alongside computer damage under Section 43 IT Act.
unresolved_ambiguity: Confirm whether dual penal/cyber charge is expected or BNS 324 alone.

query_text: In February 2024, an angry neighbor slashed the tires of a parked car and smashed the front windshield with an iron rod.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S426_E1: Intent to cause wrongful damage to property
IPC_S426_E2: Physical destruction diminishing utility of vehicle
rationale: Deliberate physical destruction of vehicle parts prior to 1 July 2024 constitutes mischief under Section 426 IPC.

query_text: In September 2024, a thief snatched an unattended backpack containing a laptop and wallet from a cafe table without the owner's knowledge or consent.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S303_E1: Dishonest intention to take movable property
BNS_S303_E2: Taken out of possession without consent
BNS_S303_E3: Moving property to complete taking
rationale: Taking movable property out of another's possession dishonestly without consent constitutes theft under Section 303 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In December 2023, a pickpocket stole a gold watch and cash from an office drawer during lunch hour without permission.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S379_E1: Dishonest intention to take movable property
IPC_S379_E2: Taken without consent out of possession
IPC_S379_E3: Moving property to effect taking
rationale: Historical movable property theft committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 379 IPC.

query_text: In August 2024, a gang threatened a shopkeeper that they would burn down his grocery store unless he paid them twenty thousand rupees every month.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S308_E1: Intentionally putting person in fear of injury/arson
BNS_S308_E2: Dishonest inducement to deliver money
rationale: Putting a merchant in fear of property destruction to induce monthly money delivery constitutes extortion under Section 308 BNS (maximum 7 years).

query_text: In January 2024, a blackmailer sent threatening letters to an executive stating he would reveal embarrassing personal secrets unless fifty thousand rupees was deposited in cash.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S384_E1: Putting person in fear of injury to reputation
IPC_S384_E2: Dishonestly demanding delivery of money
rationale: Historical extortion committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 384 IPC (maximum 3 years).

query_text: In August 2024, a gym cleaner installed a spy camera inside the female shower stall to secretly record women without their consent.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S77_E1: Capturing image of a woman in a private act
BNS_S77_E2: Reasonable expectation of privacy in shower stall
rationale: Secretly capturing images of women in private shower facilities constitutes voyeurism under Section 77 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In October 2023, a tenant secretly drilled a peephole into an adjoining bathroom to watch and photograph a female resident.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S354C_E1: Watching and capturing image of woman in private act
IPC_S354C_E2: Reasonable expectation of privacy without consent
rationale: Historical voyeurism committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 354C IPC.

query_text: In September 2024, a man repeatedly followed a woman home from the bus stop every evening for three weeks despite her yelling at him to leave her alone.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S78_E1: Perpetrator is a man and victim is a woman
BNS_S78_E2: Repeated physical following despite clear disinterest
rationale: Persistent following of a woman by a man after explicit disinterest constitutes stalking under Section 78 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In April 2024, a man sent constant unwanted text messages and monitored the social media profiles of a woman who had explicitly blocked his number.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S354D_E1: Man contacting woman despite clear disinterest
IPC_S354D_E2: Monitoring electronic communication and social media
rationale: Historical cyberstalking and unwanted electronic contact prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 354D IPC.

query_text: In August 2024, a supervisor made vulgar sexual gestures and uttered sexually explicit insults directed at a female employee in the office pantry.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S79_E1: Intention to insult modesty of a woman
BNS_S79_E2: Uttering vulgar words and making obscene gestures
rationale: Uttering sexually explicit words and making lewd gestures to insult a woman's modesty constitutes Section 79 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In May 2024, an attendee at a conference shouted lewd remarks and made indecent gestures intending to insult the modesty of a woman speaker.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S509_E1: Intention to insult modesty of woman
IPC_S509_E2: Uttering lewd words and gestures
rationale: Historical insults to female modesty committed prior to 1 July 2024 are governed by Section 509 IPC.

query_text: In August 2024, a blogger published a malicious article falsely accusing a local business owner of running an illegal drug ring, severely damaging his business.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S356_E1: Publishing written imputation
BNS_S356_E2: Imputation directly concerns identifiable individual
BNS_S356_E3: Intent or knowledge to harm reputation
rationale: Publishing false criminal allegations that harm business reputation constitutes defamation under Section 356 BNS (post-July 2024).

query_text: In November 2023, a resident circulated defamatory flyers across a residential colony alleging that a neighbor was an embezzler.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S500_E1: Making and publishing defamatory imputation
IPC_S500_E2: Intent to harm reputation
rationale: Historical defamation committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 500 IPC.

query_text: In August 2024, a moneylender threatened to physically assault a borrower and break his legs unless he surrendered his motorcycle.
legal_elements_verified: BNS_S351_E1: Threat of grievous injury to person
BNS_S351_E2: Intent to coerce surrender of property
rationale: Threatening severe bodily injury to coerce property transfer constitutes criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS (post-July 2024).
unresolved_ambiguity: Check whether extortion (BNS 308) also applies if motorcycle was handed over.

query_text: In February 2024, a landlord threatened to have thugs beat up a tenant and throw his belongings into the street if he did not vacate immediately.
legal_elements_verified: IPC_S506_E1: Threat of injury to person and property
IPC_S506_E2: Intent to compel vacating premises
rationale: Historical criminal intimidation through threats of physical violence committed prior to 1 July 2024 is governed by Section 506 IPC.

query_text: A hacker deployed ransomware that encrypted database files on a hospital server and demanded ten Bitcoin to provide the decryption key.
legal_elements_verified: ITA_S43_E3: Damaging and disrupting computer database
ITA_S66_E1: Unauthorized access under section 43
ITA_S66_E2: Dishonest and fraudulent intent
rationale: Deploying ransomware to disrupt medical databases with fraudulent intent constitutes criminal hacking under Section 66 and damage under Section 43 IT Act.

query_text: An intruder harvested credit card numbers and passwords from an e-commerce website using a keylogger script.
legal_elements_verified: ITA_S66C_E1: Misuse of password and authentication feature
ITA_S66C_E2: Credentials belong to other consumers
ITA_S66C_E3: Fraudulent and dishonest capture
rationale: Capturing and stealing customer passwords and authentication features via scripts constitutes identity theft under Section 66C IT Act.

query_text: A scammer set up a phishing website mimicking the income tax e-filing portal to trick taxpayers into revealing their banking passwords and PAN details.
legal_elements_verified: ITA_S66D_E1: Use of computer resource and internet domain
ITA_S66D_E2: Deceptive inducement of taxpayers
ITA_S66D_E3: Personating legitimate government tax portal
rationale: Operating a deceptive phishing website mimicking a government tax portal constitutes cheating by personation using computer resource under Section 66D IT Act.

query_text: A coworker shared an intimate video of a colleague's private body parts on a messaging group without her consent, recorded during a video call.
legal_elements_verified: ITA_S66E_E1: Capturing and transmitting image of private body parts
ITA_S66E_E2: Complete absence of consent
ITA_S66E_E3: Circumstances violating privacy expectation
rationale: Electronic transmission of intimate private images without consent violates privacy under Section 66E IT Act.
unresolved_ambiguity: Review if Section 67A IT Act also applies if video is sexually explicit.

query_text: A software development agency failed to deliver mobile application source code by the contractually agreed deadline despite receiving fifty percent advance payment.
rationale: Failure to complete software milestones under a commercial contract is a civil breach of contract; in the absence of initial fraudulent inducement at contract formation, it does not constitute criminal cheating.

query_text: A tenant withheld rent payment for two months citing failure of the landlord to repair water leaks in the ceiling.
rationale: Disputes regarding rent withholding and maintenance obligations fall under state Rent Control legislation and civil law, not penal or cyber statutes.

query_text: A consumer purchased a refrigerator from a retail store that stopped cooling after ten days, and the manufacturer refused to honor the warranty replacement.
rationale: Appliance warranty disputes and product defects fall under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, outside indexed criminal penal law.

query_text: An artist drew a political caricature and satirical cartoon of a government minister and published it on a social media humor page.
rationale: Political satire and humorous caricatures lack fraudulent intent and represent protected fair comment, falling outside penal defamation and cyber impersonation.

query_text: A passerby took landscape photographs of an architecturally distinctive corporate office tower from a public pavement.
rationale: Photographing a commercial building from a public street sidewalk does not violate privacy provisions (ITA 66E / BNS 77), which require bodily privacy expectations.

query_text: A pedestrian was injured in a hit-and-run collision in August 2024 where the driver sped away without reporting to the police.
rationale: Section 106(2) BNS (hit-and-run failure to report) was specifically held in abeyance by MHA Notification S.O. 850(E) and is not legally in force. Uncommenced provisions cannot be assigned as ground truth.

query_text: A cloud computing company experienced a security vulnerability where customer email addresses were leaked due to a server misconfiguration, but no penal fraud occurred.
rationale: Digital Personal Data Protection Act penalties (Section 33) remain provisional awaiting Data Protection Board operationalization; in the absence of criminal mens rea, this regulatory issue is out of penal scope.

query_text: Two corporate business partners had a disagreement regarding profit sharing ratios specified in their partnership deed and filed arbitration claims.
rationale: Partnership profit distribution disputes are governed by commercial arbitration and the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, lacking penal ingredients.

query_text: A customer received the wrong color of shoes from an online store and demanded a refund after returning the parcel.
rationale: E-commerce merchandise return and color mismatch is an ordinary commercial transaction governed by consumer sales terms, not criminal cheating.
